title: One command reads back where a run stands and who approved it
action: Expose the persisted approval state so a dashboard can read it without re-deriving anything (per D7, which scopes this feature to the data and the read surface, not the dashboard). Extend the existing status output rather than adding a new verb: build.rs already assembles the `where.gates` block (search build.rs for `gates`, near lines 128 and 217-218) from the projected booleans. Add the full gate entry beside it — state, actor, at, reason, bypass_level per gate — read from the workflow record, not from the projection, so a pending gate is visible as pending rather than as an indistinguishable false. Render one short human line per non-approved gate in the text output. The JSON shape is a published contract (docs/07-contracts.md documents bee status --json), so this is additive only: every existing key keeps its current name, type, and meaning.

truths: bee status --json exposes each gate's state, actor, at, reason, and bypass_level
A gate never approved reads as state pending, distinguishable from a gate that was rejected
Every pre-existing key in bee status --json keeps its name, type, and meaning

artifacts.substantive: gate entries read from the workflow record and emitted alongside the existing projected booleans
tests asserting the new keys and asserting the old keys are unchanged

key_links: status_full reads the workflow record's gate entries, not only the projected approved_gates booleans
prohibitions: No renaming or retyping of any existing bee status --json key
No dashboard, UI, or web surface — D7 puts it out of scope
